record.paper_title: Quadratic Stochastic Operators: Results and Open Problems
record.original_question: Develop a general dynamical-systems theory for ℓ-Volterra quadratic stochastic operators. This should include, at minimum, the construction of Lyapunov functions for ℓ-Volterra QSOs, a description of the limit sets of their trajectories, and other core structural results about their asymptotic dynamics.

evidence.quote: Problem 8. Develop theory of dynamical systems generated by a ℓ-Volterra QSO. Find its Lyapunov functions, the set of limit points of its trajectories etc.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $S^{m-1}=\{x=(x_1,\dots,x_m)\in\mathbb{R}^m: x_i\ge 0,\ \sum_{i=1}^m x_i=1\}$ denote the $(m-1)$-dimensional standard simplex. A quadratic stochastic operator (QSO) is a map $V:S^{m-1}\to S^{m-1}$ defined by
$$ (Vx)_k = \sum_{i,j=1}^{m} P_{ij,k}\, x_i x_j, \qquad k=1,\dots,m, $$
where the coefficients satisfy $P_{ij,k}=P_{ji,k}\ge 0$ and $\sum_{k=1}^m P_{ij,k}=1$ for all $i,j$.

Fix an integer $\ell\in\{0,1,\dots,m\}$. The QSO $V$ is called an $\ell$-Volterra QSO if there exists a subset $I=\{i_1,\dots,i_\ell\}\subset\{1,\dots,m\}$ of cardinality $\ell$ such that
$$ P_{ij,k}=0 \quad\text{whenever } k\notin\{i,j\}\cup I, $$
i.e. the only "non-Volterra" coordinates allowed in the support of $P_{ij,\cdot}$ lie in the distinguished set $I$. (For $\ell=0$ this recovers the classical Volterra QSOs.) Iteration of $V$ yields a discrete-time dynamical system $x^{(n+1)}=V(x^{(n)})$ on $S^{m-1}$, whose trajectory starting at $x^{(0)}$ has $\omega$-limit set $\omega(x^{(0)})$.

Develop a general theory of the dynamical systems generated by $\ell$-Volterra QSOs for arbitrary $m$ and $\ell$. In particular:

(a) Construct Lyapunov functions $\varphi:S^{m-1}\to\mathbb{R}$ (i.e. functions which are monotone along every trajectory of $V$) for general $\ell$-Volterra QSOs.

(b) Describe the structure of the set $\omega(x^{(0)})$ of limit points of trajectories for every initial point $x^{(0)}\in S^{m-1}$.

(c) Establish the further core structural results about the asymptotic behaviour of these operators (e.g.\ characterisation of fixed points, basins of attraction, ergodic properties).
artifact.status_search_result: Subsequent work (notably Rozikov–Zada, "ℓ-Volterra Quadratic Stochastic Operators: Lyapunov Functions, Trajectories", Appl. Math. Inf. Sci. 6 (2012)) constructs Lyapunov functions for ℓ-Volterra QSOs under coefficient restrictions and gives upper bounds on ω-limit sets, and describes some fixed-point sets. However, unlike pure Volterra QSOs, ω(x⁰) is not in general contained in the fixed-point set, and a complete general theory (full description of limit sets, basins, ergodic behaviour for arbitrary m and ℓ) has not been established. Hence the problem is partially solved.

status_evidence.title: ℓ-Volterra Quadratic Stochastic Operators: Lyapunov Functions, Trajectories
status_evidence.snippet: Under certain conditions on coefficients of ℓ-Volterra QSOs we describe Lyapunov functions… apply them to obtain upper estimates for the set of ω-limit points of trajectories.
status_evidence.claim: Lyapunov functions and partial description of ω-limit sets have been obtained for ℓ-Volterra QSOs under coefficient restrictions.

status_evidence.title: Dynamics of Infinite Dimensional Lotka–Volterra Operators
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work continues to investigate dynamics of Volterra-type operators on simplices.
status_evidence.claim: Research on related Volterra operator dynamics is ongoing as of 2025, indicating the general ℓ-Volterra theory is still incomplete.

status_evidence.title: On a Superposition of Volterra and Permuted Volterra Quadratic Stochastic Operators
status_evidence.snippet: Studies of variants of Volterra QSOs continue to appear.
status_evidence.claim: The general dynamical theory remains an active topic with only partial results.
